senses.sense_definition: An inquiry or investigation into the truth of some matter.

examples.text: The committee launched a formal <w>inquisition</w> into the company's financial records.
After a thorough <w>inquisition</w> of the facts, the truth finally emerged.

senses.sense_definition: A harsh or rigorous interrogation that violates one’s rights.

examples.text: The suspect felt that the police questioning had turned into a cruel <w>inquisition</w>.
She refused to answer the reporter's aggressive <w>inquisition</w> about her private life.

senses.sense_definition: The finding of a jury, especially such a finding under a writ of inquiry.

examples.text: The court reviewed the <w>inquisition</w> delivered by the jury regarding the property dispute.
Legal experts analyzed the <w>inquisition</w> to determine if the jury followed proper procedure.

senses.sense_definition: A historical tribunal of the Roman Catholic Church set up to investigate and suppress heresy.

examples.text: Many people were persecuted during the <w>Inquisition</w> for their religious beliefs.
Historians study the <w>Inquisition</w> to understand the power of the church in the Middle Ages.

senses.sense_definition: To make an inquiry concerning; to investigate into.

examples.text: The authorities began to <w>inquisition</w> the witnesses about the missing documents.
It is not the role of the press to <w>inquisition</w> private citizens without cause.
